findings.title: Microsoft fixes bug that removed Copilot buttons in Outlook
findings.summary_md: Microsoft fixed a known issue that removed the Copilot Chat or Copilot buttons in classic Outlook for Windows users with a Copilot Chat (Basic) license. The Outlook Team addressed it with a service change on June 29, 2026 and advised affected users to restart the client, update to the latest build, or revert to Current Channel build 16.0.20026.20168, or use new Outlook or OWA. Copilot remained available through Outlook on the web and the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.

findings.title: Microsoft says Copilot buttons still missing in classic Outlook
findings.summary_md: Microsoft said it was still investigating the known issue after classic Outlook for Windows was updated to build 20026.20182 or higher, which removed Copilot and Copilot Chat buttons for users with Copilot Chat (Basic) or paid M365 Copilot (Premium) accounts. Microsoft traced it to Outlook being unable to locate the MAPI property PR_PROFILE_USER_SMTP_EMAIL_ADDRESS_W in the null profile section, preventing Copilot settings from persisting. A temporary workaround was enabling Show Apps in Outlook under File, Options, Advanced, or creating a new profile or using OWA.

findings.title: Copilot buttons are missing in classic Outlook for Windows
findings.summary_md: Microsoft's support document lists the issue as fixed, stating classic Outlook for Windows builds 20026.20182 and higher could fail to show Copilot Chat or Copilot entry points for users with a Copilot Chat (Basic) license or paid M365 Copilot (Premium) account. The root cause was a bug that prevented Outlook from retrieving required account information from the user's Outlook profile. Workarounds included using new Outlook or OWA or creating a new Outlook profile, and Microsoft noted the button can also be hidden by licensing, app configuration, update channel, privacy settings, or other factors.
